18 games 57 stories 7 new this week Facts only Gold tag = older but still relevant

This week at a glance

  • Dune: Imperium – Conspiracy (Oct 22): Dire Wolf gave the full rundown (Conspiracy cards, Raids, Imperial Edicts, Stoneburners, Overthrow Mode, 6 leaders) and said pre-orders open on its shop Oct 26 at $40 with a Shadow Council promo. At about 8:45 a.m. ET the shop still said “opening soon.”
  • Dice Throne Nexus: The Kickstarter stood at $1,721,084 from 11,531 backers on Oct 26 (up from $1.48M). It ends Nov 3–4. The FAQ puts Digital Beta Wave 2 in late Nov / early Dec 2026.
  • StarCraft TMG (Oct 25, community): Wave 3 boxes reached one German retailer early. Official shipping still starts Nov 2 (EU) / Nov 9 (rest of world).
  • Star Wars: Rebellion (checked Oct 26): The core set now shows Sold out at Asmodee USA; Rise of the Empire is still orderable. There is no out-of-print notice.
  • Imperial Assault (rechecked Oct 26): The Core Set is still Sold out at Asmodee USA, and Tyrants of Lothal is orderable. There is still no official out-of-print notice.
  • Star Trek Ascendancy: Final Frontier: The latest three Gamefound updates are #48 (Oct 5, Unboxing! Shipping Imminent!), #47 (Aug 28, Starbases), and #46 (Aug 21, Gorn plastics). There was still no Update 49 on Oct 26.
  • Captain’s Chair & King of Tokyo at SPIEL: Frosted Games showed the German editions (Zweiter Kontakt due Q4 2026). IELLO ran King of Tokyo: Godzilla and Duel: Tokyo Bay tournaments on Oct 24.
  • Special watch: Marvel Legendary What If…? Season 2: No change. There is still no official Upper Deck status post, and a Canadian pre-order listing remains live.

Dice Throne

Dice-battling heroes · Roxley / Dice Throne

Nexus Kickstarter passes $1.72M from 11,500+ backers with about a week left; FAQ moves Digital Beta Wave 2 to late Nov / early Dec 2026

Stats Oct 26, 2026 · FAQ updated Oct 14–15 New this week

Kickstarter’s public stats on the morning of Oct 26 (about 8:40 a.m. ET) showed $1,721,084 from 11,531 backers, up from $1,480,349 and 10,027 backers on Oct 19. Trackers put the average pledge at about $149. Last year’s Vanguard campaign finished at $1,784,099. The campaign closes at 2 a.m. UK time on Nov 4 (evening of Nov 3 in ET).

The campaign FAQ (updated Oct 14–15) says Beta Wave 2 of Dice Throne Digital starts in late November / early December 2026; an earlier “2027” date was a typo. Kickstarter exclusives listed there: a metal prone token for Snyper, acrylic fuel-cell tokens for Punch-A-Tron, lenticular emotes for Hacker, and acrylic Ghost Step standees for Phantom Runner. A $1 pledge gives pledge-manager access. Stretch Pay is not enabled.

Sources: Kickstarter · Kickstarter FAQ · Tabletop Analytics · PledgeBox tracker

Nexus Kickstarter is live: funded in five minutes, about $1.48M from 10,000+ backers by Oct 19

Launched Oct 13 · reported Oct 15 · stats Oct 19 Carried forward · last week

Dice Throne Nexus went live on Kickstarter on Oct 13. Backseat Gamer (Oct 15), citing the launch-day update, reports that the campaign cleared its $50,000 goal in five minutes and passed $1.08M from 7,100+ backers by the next morning. Kickstarter’s public stats on the morning of Oct 19 showed $1,480,349 from 10,027 backers. For comparison, last year’s Vanguard campaign finished at $1,784,099 from 16,465 backers.

Pledges as reported: about $60 (Limited Edition Nexus StrongBox with upgrades for the four heroes, eight Mythic cards, and four promos), about $145 (adds four Accessory Packs and the SAGAS: The Crimson Code co-op box; the most popular tier), and about $295 (everything, including playmats, an alt-art hero board set, and a dice tray). Estimated delivery: September 2027. The campaign closes at 2 a.m. UK time on Nov 4 (evening of Nov 3 in ET). Campaign materials name the fourth hero Phantom Runner; earlier coverage called this hero “Ghostrunner.”

Sources: Kickstarter · Backseat Gamer (Oct 15) · Games Press release

Dice Throne SAGAS: The Crimson Code revealed: story-driven co-op for 1–4 players

Oct 9, 2026 (Screen Rant exclusive) Older · still relevant

Screen Rant’s Oct 9 exclusive (not covered last week) introduced Dice Throne SAGAS, a new story-driven line that starts with The Crimson Code, part of the Nexus campaign. It is playable solo or with up to three others. The Mad King returns inside a VR world called the Nexus. Play runs across a comic-book-style booklet board in five acts with boss fights. New red and blue “byte” tokens replace a long list of separate status effects, and heroes level up at 10 XP. Existing heroes can be brought in. The designers say it draws on Adventures and Marvel Missions.

Source: Screen Rant (Oct 9)

2026 Rules Updates: “Buh, Bye!” returns to Organized Play; new timing rules from Jan 1, 2027

Oct 5, 2026 Older · still relevant

Dice Throne’s official blog (Oct 5, not covered last week) says the Instant Action card Buh, Bye!, banned in Organized Play since January 2025, will no longer be banned from the Age that begins in January 2027 and “must now be used in all Hero decks.” A set of clarified timing rules for interrupting Actions takes effect Jan 1, 2027. The post says the core rules and “Golden Rules” are unchanged and most standard games will not feel different.

Source: Dice Throne blog (Oct 5)

StarCraft Miniatures Game

StarCraft: Tabletop Miniatures Game · Archon Studio (Blizzard license)

Community report: some Wave 3 boxes reached a German retailer early; official shipping still starts Nov 2 (EU)

Oct 25, 2026 (community) New this week

Fan site sc-tabletop-news.de (Oct 25) reports that a Reddit user in Germany got Wave 3 boxes (Tassadar, High Templar, Defiler, and Zagara with the Bile Launcher) early from the retailer Fantasy Welt. This is a community report of one retailer, not an Archon announcement.

Archon’s official schedule is unchanged: shipping starts Nov 2 in Europe and Nov 9 for the rest of the world, and it runs over several weeks. No new Archon or starcraft-tmg.com StarCraft post appeared between Oct 19 and Oct 26.

Sources: sc-tabletop-news.de (Oct 25) · Official pre-order post (Oct 9)

Wave 3 Terran rules preview: Raven (first flying-stand unit) and two Nova Terra loadouts

Oct 19, 2026 Carried forward · last week

Archon Studio’s Oct 19 development post previews the Terran half of Wave 3. The Raven is described as the game’s first airborne unit on a dedicated flight stand: a support drone built around an Advanced Sensor Array (detection), automated deployment systems, and target painting rather than front-line damage. Nova Terra is a Hero with two loadouts: Stealth Mode (C-20A Canister Rifle, Stealth Suit, long-range picks) and Assault Mode (Hellfire Shotgun and Monomolecular Blade for close combat).

This completes a three-post series this week covering every Wave 3 faction (Zerg Oct 14, Protoss Oct 16, Terran Oct 19). Pre-orders opened Oct 12; official shipping starts Nov 2 (Europe) and Nov 9 (rest of world).

Sources: Archon blog (Oct 19) · StarCraft TMG rules post

Wave 3 Protoss rules preview: Tassadar’s Force Walls and the High Templar

Oct 16, 2026 Carried forward · last week

Archon’s Oct 16 post covers the Protoss Wave 3 additions. Tassadar is a support Hero focused on board control: Force Walls block movement paths and can inflict damage that bypasses armour rolls when enemies move through or around them. Khala’s Gift reduces the cost of a friendly Biological unit’s first Special Ability each round, and Executor’s Will lets him mark two enemy units in the Assault Phase. The post also previews the High Templar unit.

Sources: Archon blog (Oct 16) · StarCraft TMG rules post

Wave 3 Zerg rules preview: Defiler (Dark Swarm, Consume, Plague), Zagara, and a Bile Launcher structure

Oct 14, 2026 Carried forward · last week

Archon’s Oct 14 post details the Zerg side. The Defiler (40 mm base) brings Dark Swarm (a token that lets nearby friendly units make evade rolls in the assault phase, with +1 for size-one units), Consume (destroy a nearby friendly model to cut biomass costs), and Plague (a blast template of non-lethal damage that scales with biomass spent). Broodmother Zagara grants a once-per-round bonus to units of a chosen size and can use her base as an entry edge (Infested Drop).

Zagara’s box also includes a Bile Launcher: a placeable artillery structure (within 18″ of your entry edge) with Bombard that does not need line of sight. Archon says it is the first structure that can hold objective markers. A Zagara’s Swarm faction card and a Reactive Creep card are also included.

Sources: Archon blog (Oct 14) · StarCraft TMG rules post

October 2026 balance changelog: Terran Stimpack units cost more, Zerg infantry cheaper

Changelog dated Oct 9, 2026 Older · still relevant

Archon’s official changelog dated 09.10.2026 (not covered in last week’s report) adjusts unit and tactical-card costs “to encourage greater variety in army compositions,” with “particular attention to Zerg.” Terran: Marine (160/210 → 170/220), Marauder, Medic (110 → 120), and Jim Raynor (250 → 280) go up; Barracks and Academy cost more gas; Dropship and Goliath get cheaper. Zerg: Zergling (180/220 → 150/210), Raptor, Swarmling (260 → 210), Queen, Roach variants, Hydralisk upgrades, and several tactical cards get cheaper. Protoss: Zealot, Adept, Artanis, and Nexus go up; Praetor Guard, Stalker, Sentry upgrades, and Twilight Council go down.

A matching October 2026 cost table is posted on the official downloads page.

Sources: Changelog PDF (Oct 9) · Cost table PDF · Official downloads page

Wave 3 pre-orders open Oct 12: Nova, Tassadar, Zagara, Raven, High Templar, Defiler, faction dice

Pre-orders open Oct 12, 2026 · announced Oct 9 Older · still relevant

Archon Studio’s Oct 9 post says the next StarCraft: Tabletop Miniatures Game wave opens for pre-order on Oct 12. Heroes: Terran Ghost Nova Terra, Protoss Executor Tassadar, and Zerg Broodmother Zagara. Support units: Terran Raven, Protoss High Templar, and Zerg Defiler. The wave also adds custom faction dice sets for Terran, Protoss, and Zerg. Prices were not listed in the announcement.

Shipping schedule from the official post: Europe begins Nov 2; rest of world begins Nov 9. Those dates mark the start of fulfillment, not when every order will have shipped. This follows Wave 2 (Siege Tank, Immortal, Zeratul, Ravager), which had first player reviews the week of Oct 1.

Sources: Official StarCraft TMG (Oct 9) · Backseat Gamer (Oct 11)

Dune Imperium

Dire Wolf · Imperium / Uprising / Immortality and related expansions

Dire Wolf: “Conspiracy is Coming Soon!” Full rundown, and pre-orders on Dire Wolf’s shop from Oct 26

Oct 22, 2026 New this week

Dire Wolf’s Oct 22 post is the first detailed official look at Dune: Imperium – Conspiracy, an expansion for both Dune: Imperium and Uprising. It adds Conspiracy cards (drafted at setup and paid for with spice or Conspiracy chips), Raids (spend swords during your Reveal turn to conquer planets, with consequences for factions), and optional modules: Imperial Edicts, Stoneburners (a one-time reset of the Imperium row / raid tokens), Spy tokens for base Imperium, and a new Swordmaster space (8/6 Solari). Dire Wolf lists 6 new Leaders, 46 new Imperium cards, the return of Graft, and Overthrow Mode (Paul vs. two or three conspirators who pool their victory points).

The post says pre-orders open on Dire Wolf’s shop on Monday, Oct 26. As of about 8:45 a.m. ET that day the shop page ($40.00) still said “Pre-orders opening soon!” with both shipping options unavailable. Pre-orders there include a Shadow Council promo card. Asmodee Deutschland lists the German release as late November 2026.

Sources: Dire Wolf (Oct 22) · Dire Wolf shop

Conspiracy expansion on Q4 2026 retail track; US preorders listing ~Oct 31–Nov 15

Announced Aug 24, 2026 Older · active preorders

ICv2 reported Dire Wolf’s Conspiracy expansion for Q4 2026 retail. It is compatible with both Dune: Imperium and Uprising, adding lasting Conspiracy cards, planet raids, Imperial Edicts, and asymmetric Overthrow Mode (one Emperor vs. two or three opponents). GameNerdz lists an expected release of Oct 31, 2026 at $40 (SKU DWD01024); As of last week’s check GameNerdz said Oct 31, Miniature Market said “November 2026”, and Atomic Empire listed Nov 15. Dire Wolf’s Oct 22 post (above) gives no day-level retail date. Dates may still move.

Sources: ICv2 · GameNerdz · Atomic Empire

Digital 4.1.0 adds online Reputation system (Sept 30)

Sept 30, 2026 Older · still relevant

Dire Wolf shipped Dune: Imperium Digital patch 4.1.0 with a Reputation system aimed at early leavers: players start at 30 Rep, gain Rep for finishing games (wins not required), lose Rep for leaving early, and can set lobby minimums. Rep below 0 blocks Ranked until rebuilt. The patch also includes gameplay, UI, mobile, and achievement fixes.

Source: Dire Wolf Digital

Resistance is Futile and Duty and Honor announced; retail timing disagrees

Retail target: August 2027 (ICv2) · WizKids shop: Q3 2027 Upcoming

WizKids opened pre-orders for two 2027 Captain’s Chair boxes. Resistance is Futile (ICv2: $59.99; Coqui Hobby item code WZK87655) is a standalone 1–2 player game, ages 14+, 60–120 minutes, with Captain Janeway, Seven of Nine, Locutus, and the Borg Queen, plus the U.S.S. Voyager and a Borg Cube. Duty and Honor ($39.99; Coqui WZK87656) is an expansion adding Worf, Gul Dukat, and two captains WizKids has not named, plus ships including the Val Jean and the U.S.S. Defiant. It requires the original Captain’s Chair, To Boldly Go, or Resistance is Futile. ICv2 (Sept 9) and Coqui Hobby (Sept 29) both say August 2027 retail. WizKids’ own shop, checked Oct 3, 2026, lists both as pre-orders with estimated release Q3 2027 ($59.99 and $39.99) and says pre-order dates can change. ScreenRant (Sept 20), citing CW, instead dates Duty and Honor to November 2027 while keeping Resistance is Futile in Q3 2027. Treat August vs. November as unresolved until WizKids publishes a day-level street date.

Sources: ICv2 (Sept 9) · Coqui Hobby (Sept 29) · WizKids Resistance is Futile · WizKids Duty and Honor · ScreenRant (Sept 20) · Backseat Gamer (Sept 12)

To Boldly Go standalone is on the WizKids shop at $59.99

Checked Oct 3, 2026 · publisher date Jul 15, 2026 Status check

To Boldly Go is a fully standalone 1–2 player set (ages 14+, about 60–120 minutes) with solo play and six asymmetric captain decks. Publisher copy names Kirk, Khan (Asmodee UK spells it “Kahn”), Philippa Georgiou from Discovery, and Rebner, the Pakled commander from Lower Decks, and says the box has six captains total. Asmodee UK lists a publisher release date of July 15, 2026 (RRP £59.99). On Oct 3, 2026 the WizKids U.S. shop showed an Add to cart button at $59.99 rather than a pre-order hold. Earlier July coverage had described a July ship window with some channels back-ordered; confirm local stock.

Sources: WizKids shop (checked Oct 3) · Asmodee UK (Jul 15, 2026) · Bleeding Cool (Jul 25) · ScreenRant (Jul 16)

Second Contact expansion ($29.99) adds Pike, Freeman, and Krulmuth-B

Checked Oct 3, 2026 Status check

Second Contact is an expansion, not a standalone. WizKids states it requires Star Trek: Captain’s Chair or To Boldly Go (the shop page does not list Resistance is Futile as a host). It adds Carol Freeman of the U.S.S. Cerritos, Christopher Pike, and at least one more captain (“and more”; the contents list three crew boards), plus Krulmuth-B as a starting location. Listed contents include 99 standard cards, 9 ship tokens, and 6 automated command cards. On Oct 3, 2026 the WizKids shop showed Add to cart at $29.99. The original Captain’s Chair (Picard, Sisko, Michael Burnham, Koloth, Sela, Thy’lek Shran) was also Add to cart at $59.99 the same day.

Sources: WizKids Second Contact · WizKids base game · Backseat Gamer

Star Trek Ascendancy: Final Frontier

Gale Force Nine · Gamefound campaign / all-in collection

Gamefound Update 48 (latest): “Unboxing! Shipping Imminent!” (still no Update 49 as of Oct 26)

Update Oct 5, 2026 · rechecked Oct 26 This window

Newest of the latest three Gamefound updates. GF9’s New Zealand studio unboxed a finished Deluxe All-In copy (game and civilization boxes, rulebooks, trays, space lanes, planet discs, and all civilizations, including Borg, Gorn, Tholian, Terran, Vulcan, and others). GF9 says partners are “putting the finishing touches” and all pledges should be “on the water and on the way to distribution centers imminently,” which keeps to the early-August timeline: distributors in Q4 2026, backer fulfillment likely early Q1 2027.

As of Oct 26, three weeks after it was posted, the Gamefound updates list still shows Update 48 as the newest post. The promised follow-up with container-loading photos (“much sooner rather than later”) had not appeared. Gamefound blocks automated readers, so this check relied on the public updates index and search snapshots.

Sources: Gamefound update 48 (Oct 5) · Updates index · Aug 6 timeline (update 44)

Production Update: August 2026 (Week 4) — plastic Starbases; factory exit expected September

Update Aug 28, 2026 Older · still relevant

GF9’s Week 4 August update closed the weekly plastics series with photos of new full-color plastic Starbases for the existing civilizations (Federation, Klingon, Romulan, Ferengi, Andorian, Cardassian, Breen, Dominion). Production was described as still on pace with the earlier August timeline (factory-to-distributor start in Q3; distributors in Q4 2026; backer fulfillment likely early Q1 2027). GF9 said the next bulletin would come in September once goods leave the factory for distribution hubs—hoped within a couple of weeks of the update, possibly sliding toward late September—after which more concrete regional fulfillment dates would follow. The promised follow-up came on Oct 5 as update 48 (above), a few days after the September target.

Sources: Gamefound Week 4 (Aug 28) · Aug 6 timeline · Campaign page

Production Update: August 2026 (Week 3) — Gorn plastics and printed Civilization Box

Update Aug 21, 2026 Older · still relevant

Week 3 showcased advance Gorn civilization plastics photographed at GF9’s New Zealand studio and gave a first look at the fully printed Civilization Box (Borg Cube–styled packaging). GF9 said production remained on pace with the August timeline and previewed that the following week would cover plastic Starbases.

Source: Gamefound Week 3 (Aug 21)

Press: Gamers Together recaps Update 48 (“finally close to shipping”); no new dates

Oct 15, 2026 This window

Czech site Gamers Together (Oct 15, not covered last week) recaps Update 48 and GF9’s August timeline (production-to-distributor shipments from Q3, stock with regional partners in Q4 2026, backer fulfillment likely early Q1 2027, all approximate). It repeats the March 2026 explanation (more than 3.5 million pieces) and lists what Final Frontier adds: Gorn, Tholian, and Terran Empire civilizations, a 15-scenario Campaign Mode, Non-Player Civilizations for solo play, revised rules, and storage. Its header says “Ships at last,” but the article gives no new dates beyond GF9’s own updates.

Source: Gamers Together (Oct 15)

Press roundup: Game Rant and The News recap Update 48; no new information from GF9

Oct 14, 2026 Carried forward · last week

Game Rant and The News (Pakistan) both published Oct 14 articles recapping Update 48: a finished Deluxe All-In copy was unboxed in New Zealand, pledges are expected “on the water” imminently, distributors should receive stock in Q4 2026, and final fulfillment is likely early Q1 2027. Both cite GF9’s March 2026 statement that the project needs more than 3.5 million individual pieces. Neither article adds new dates beyond GF9’s own updates.

Sources: Game Rant (Oct 14) · The News (Oct 14)

Blood Rage

Area control · Tycoon Games (Godly series; formerly CMON)

No new news this week. Rechecked Oct 26: Asmodee USA still dates Valhalla ($124.99) and Road to Helheim ($89.99) for Nov 6, and both can be ordered. Tycoon’s newest Gamefound update is still the Sept 25 mid-fulfillment report. No official Valhalla FAQ or errata has been published.

Valhalla U.S. retail dated Nov 6 at Asmodee USA ($124.99); Add to cart live

Checked Oct 12, 2026 · releases Nov 6 Older · still relevant

Asmodee USA lists Blood Rage: Valhalla (Tycoon Games) at $124.99 with a release date of Nov 6, 2026. On Oct 12 the page had a working Add to cart button. Asmodee UK lists an RRP of £124.99. Contents include 30 warrior, 10 elite, and 16 monster miniatures, 165 cards, and the Rainbow Bridge module that can link a game of original Blood Rage to a Valhalla session.

Gamefound backer fulfillment (update 31, Sept 25) already finished U.S. pledges; other regions were still shipping. Retail is the next wave for non-backers.

Sources: Asmodee USA Valhalla · Backseat Gamer (Oct 10) · Gamefound update 31

Road to Helheim also dated Nov 6 at Asmodee USA ($89.99)

Checked Oct 12, 2026 · releases Nov 6 Older · still relevant

Asmodee USA also lists Blood Rage: Valhalla – Road to Helheim at $89.99 with the same Nov 6, 2026 release date and a working Add to cart button. The listing describes the Ram Clan, three gods, and 12 monsters. Last week’s Cardhaus estimate of Nov 30 is superseded for Asmodee USA by this official Nov 6 date. Asmodee USA additionally lists a Divine Devastation oversized-god kit at $124.99.

Sources: Asmodee USA Road to Helheim · Asmodee USA Divine Devastation · Backseat Gamer (Oct 10)

Valhalla fulfillment: U.S. backers done; Canada, Europe, Australia shipping; UK in weeks

Update Sept 25, 2026 Older · still relevant

Tycoon’s Sept 25 “Mid Fulfillment Update” (Gamefound update 31) says U.S. fulfillment of Blood Rage: Valhalla is finished. Shipments are going out to backers in Canada, Europe/rest of world, and Australia. UK fulfillment should finish “within the next couple of weeks,” and China is still preparing. This follows the Sept 7 update saying the game was ready to ship.

The same post teases a new Gamefound campaign from “the creators of Blood Rage”: Rage of the Feathered Serpent, based on Mesoamerican mythology. So far there is only a page to follow, with no date or price.

Sources: Gamefound update 31 (Sept 25) · Gamefound update 30 (Sept 7)

Tycoon Games’ remastered Blood Rage: 2nd Edition folds the formerly exclusive Stag Clan and five-player support into the core box. Base game still in Asmodee catalog (Bauza & Cathala two-player)

Release: Oct 2024 (Repos / Asmodee) Older, still relevant

The Lord of the Rings: Duel for Middle-earth is the Repos Production two-player game from Antoine Bauza and Bruno Cathala. Players choose Fellowship or Sauron across three chapters and can win immediately via the Quest of the Ring, six Race alliances, or presence across all seven regions. Asmodee USA lists the English base set (7DUME-EN01) at $39.99; on Oct 5 the direct store had a working Add to cart button.

Sources: Asmodee USA · Repos Production

Allies expansion in retail since October 24, 2025

Retail: Oct 24, 2025 Older, still relevant

Repos / Asmodee’s Allies mini-expansion for Duel for Middle-earth reached retail on October 24, 2025 (ICv2). Each side gains Ally cards (7 Fellowship / 7 Sauron) plus Power tokens and player aids; players start with secret Allies and spend tokens for enter/exit effects. Requires the base game. Repos press materials describe 14 Vincent Dutrait-illustrated Ally cards and 8 Power tokens.

Sources: ICv2 · Repos Allies press · Asmodee CA product

Star Wars: Deckbuilding Game

Deckbuilding · Fantasy Flight Games / Asmodee

No new news this week. No new FFG posts for the line this week.

Rebel & Empire Reinforcements Expansion in retail since July 24

Released Jul 24, 2026 Older · still in market

FFG/Asmodee’s Rebel & Empire Reinforcements Expansion (SWG04, $34.99) reached U.S. retail on July 24, 2026 and remained orderable at Asmodee USA on Oct 26 and at local retailers (select markets). The 140-card expansion for the original Rebel vs. Empire edition adds mission cards that unlock set-aside reinforcements (Yoda, R2-D2, Emperor Palpatine, Admiral Thrawn, Home One, Executor, and more), new bases, upgraded starter cards, and three new modes including a five-part campaign. Requires the original edition (SWG01); not compatible as a standalone with Clone Wars Edition alone.

Sources: FFG Available Now · FFG announcement (Apr 23) · Asmodee USA · ICv2

Designer diaries: missions and Upgraded Starter Mode

Jul 9 & May 14, 2026 Older · design context

Lead designer Caleb Grace detailed how mission cards let each faction earn 25 reinforcements without bloating the galaxy deck (Mission Briefing, May 14), and how campaign scoring led to an optional Upgraded Starter Mode that swaps in stronger starter cards and higher-HP mission-linked bases for a more aggressive one-off game (A Fresh Start, Jul 9). No newer product announcement for the line appeared between late July and this Oct 26 search.

Sources: A Fresh Start (FFG) · Mission Briefing (FFG) · FFG tag feed

Mandalorian Faction Pack still the live fifth-faction add-on

Released Nov 28, 2025 Older · product line context

The Mandalorian Faction Pack (SWG03) shipped November 28, 2025 and remains the line’s faction add-on: base/starter/galaxy cards for a fifth playable faction plus rules and neutrals for a three-player free-for-all. It requires either the original or Clone Wars Edition core. Together with Reinforcements (original-edition expansion) and Clone Wars Edition, it is the current published footprint—no core reprints or further packs were newly announced through Oct 26.

Sources: FFG announcement · FFG Available Now (Nov 28) · FFG product page (SWG04)

Marvel Legendary

Legendary: A Marvel Deck Building Game · Upper Deck

What If…? Season 2 status watch: no change; still no official Upper Deck status post

Retailer dates cited ~mid-2026 · rechecked Oct 26 Older, still relevant

Distributor and retailer listings for Legendary What If…? Season 2 (UDE81752 / UD81752) still describe a ~100-card expansion continuing the Marvel Studios What If…? line (Kahhori, Happy “The Freak” Hogan, Avengers Across Time, keywords such as Reshape and Showoff). Some mid-2026 expected-ship dates on those listings have now passed without a matching Upper Deck “available now” announcement. Community speculation about delays or cancellation exists, but this report found no official Upper Deck notice that the expansion is discontinued—treat retail dates as unconfirmed and verify stock locally. Oct 26 recheck: Upper Deck has still not posted an official status, delay, or cancellation notice for What If…? Season 2. Its news feed (newest post Oct 20, Rush of Ikorr) has no Legendary items. Hobbiesville still lists the set as a Pre Order at CA$26.95, available to order. A search of X for Oct 19–26 found no posts about the set. Some web search summaries describe the set as “cancelled,” but they trace back to retailer and distributor reports, not Upper Deck. A June 2026 BGG thread reported an LGS email that distributors cancelled a pre-order, but that is not an Upper Deck statement—this digest will not call the set discontinued without an official source.

Sources: Southern Hobby · Hobbiesville · GTS Distribution

Core Set Second Edition released June 17 with Miles Morales and Doc Ock

Release: June 17, 2026 Older, still relevant

Upper Deck’s Legendary: A Marvel Deck Building Game Second Edition (distributor code UDC99110) shipped June 17, 2026 as a redesigned core—not a reprint. The set grows to 550 playable cards (~250 reworked), adds Doctor Octopus as a Mastermind with the Sinister Syndicate Villain Group, and puts Spider-Man (Miles Morales) in the core in place of Deadpool. Masterminds are double-sided (normal/Epic), Schemes go to nine, Bystanders to 42, and 4–5 player games gain a Warmup Round. Full-bleed original art on every card; compatible with the existing Marvel Legendary expansion library. Street price listings cluster around $99.95.

Sources: Upper Deck What’s New · Upper Deck product hub · ICv2 (Feb 6) · Backseat Gamer · LegendaryCardGame expansions
